SEATTLE GENERAL HOSPITAL

Department of Internal Medicine

Seattle, WA 98101 | (206) 555-0100

COMPREHENSIVE MEDICAL REPORT

Report ID MEDRPT-2024-0347 Date of Service October 26, 2024

PATIENT INFORMATION

Field Value
Patient Name Jonathan Michael Harrison
Date of Birth March 15, 1978
Patient ID PAT-3847-2024
Attending Physician Dr. Elizabeth Warren, MD
Primary Physician Dr. Elizabeth Warren, MD
Insurance BlueCross BlueShield
Member ID BCB-445782

VITAL SIGNS

Measurement Value Normal Range Status
Blood Pressure 142/88 100-140 mmHg ELEVATED
Heart Rate 92 bpm 60-100 bpm NORMAL
Temperature 98.6°F 97.0-98.9°F NORMAL
Respiratory Rate 18 breaths/min 12-20 breaths/min NORMAL
O2 Saturation 98% 95-100% NORMAL

CHIEF COMPLAINT

Patient presents with persistent headaches occurring 3-4 times per week for the past 6 weeks, rated 6-7/10 in severity. Associated symptoms include occasional dizziness, mild nausea, and sensitivity to light. Patient reports increased stress at work and difficulty sleeping. No history of migraines. Blood pressure slightly elevated today.

MEDICAL HISTORY

  • Hypertension (diagnosed 2019) - controlled with Lisinopril 10mg daily
  • Type 2 Diabetes (diagnosed 2021) - managed with Metformin 500mg twice daily
  • Appendectomy (2005) - no complications
  • No known drug allergies
  • Family history: Father - heart disease, Mother - diabetes

CURRENT MEDICATIONS

  1. Lisinopril 10mg - once daily for hypertension
  2. Metformin 500mg - twice daily for diabetes
  3. Aspirin 81mg - once daily for cardiovascular protection
  4. Vitamin D3 2000 IU - once daily

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

  • General: alert and oriented, no acute distress
  • HEENT: Normocephalic, pupils equal and reactive, no exophthalmos
  • Neck: Supple, no thyromegaly, no cervical lymphadenopathy
  • Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops
  • Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezes or rales
  • Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, normoactive bowel sounds
  • Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, normal strength and sensation
  • Extremities: No edema, erythema, or clubbing

LABORATORY RESULTS

Test Result Reference Range Flag
Glucose Fasting 118 mg/dL 70-100 mg/dL HIGH
HbA1c 6.8% <5.7% HIGH
Total Cholesterol 210 mg/dL <200 mg/dL HIGH
Triglycerides 165 mg/dL <150 mg/dL HIGH
HDL Cholesterol 48 mg/dL >40 mg/dL
LDL Cholesterol 135 mg/dL <100 mg/dL HIGH
TSH 2.1 mIU/L 0.4-4.0 mIU/L
eGFR 82 mL/min >60 mL/min
Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL 0.6-1.2 mg/dL
Hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL 13.5-17.5 g/dL
WBC 7.2K/uL 4.5K-11.0K uL
Platelets 250 K/uL 150-400 K/uL

IMAGING STUDIES

CT Head without Contrast (12/20/2024): FINDINGS: No acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass effect, or midline shift. Ventricles normal in size and configuration. No abnormal areas of restricted diffusion. No acute extra-axial fluid collections. Paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells well aerated.

IMPRESSION: Normal CT head examination. No acute intracranial pathology identified.

ASSESSMENT

  1. Tension-type headaches - likely secondary to stress and your sleep
  2. Hypertension, Stage 1 - inadequately controlled
  3. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus - fair control (HbA1c 6.8%)
  4. Hyperlipidemia - LDL above target
